sceneEn: You have injured yourself doing sport and come to the emergency department. Say how it happened, what you have hurt and how it feels now.
partnerEn: a nurse working fast in the emergency department
openingEn: What happened? Where does it hurt?
goalEn: How the accident happened and what was injured have been described, the nurse has said the next step and the patient has repeated it.

sceneEn: You have come to a new practice for the first time. The receptionist is asking about your insurance and your card; answer, and ask whether the appointment is free.
partnerEn: a fast-talking receptionist at the desk
openingEn: Good afternoon. Have you been to us before? Which health insurer are you with?
goalEn: The insurance details have been given, any problem with the card has been mentioned and the question of cost has been settled.

sceneEn: Your tooth has been hurting all night and you are ringing the practice in the morning. Describe the pain, say how urgent it is and ask whether you can come in today.
partnerEn: a receptionist on the phone working from the appointment book
openingEn: Berger dental practice, good morning. What can I do for you?
goalEn: The pain and the urgency have been described, a time has been agreed and the patient has repeated that time.

sceneEn: You have been going through a very stressful few weeks and you are talking to a friend. Say what is wearing you out and what helps you.
partnerEn: a friend who listens and comes up with suggestions
openingEn: You've seemed so on edge lately. Is everything all right with you?
goalEn: The cause of the stress has been described, at least one way of unwinding has been discussed and you have decided to try one of them.

sceneEn: You are talking to your doctor at your annual check-up. Say what you do to stay healthy, and listen to and confirm the doctor's advice.
partnerEn: a GP who takes preventive care seriously
openingEn: Your results look good. So what do you do for your health?
goalEn: What the patient does has been described, the doctor has given at least one piece of advice and the patient has repeated it in their own words.

sceneEn: Your neighbour is at the door and wants to borrow something. Give it to them, say when they should bring it back and add one thing they should be careful about.
partnerEn: a neighbour who has come to the door in a hurry
openingEn: Sorry, could you lend me something for a moment?
goalEn: An item has been lent, a time to return it has been agreed and the neighbour has said thank you.

sceneEn: Some things have been left behind in the classroom after a course. You and the teacher are working out one by one whose they are.
partnerEn: a course teacher pointing at the things one by one
openingEn: A few things have been left here. Whose is this?
goalEn: At least three items have been talked through, one has turned out to be yours and it has been decided what happens to the rest.

sceneEn: Your flatmate is ringing you and wants you to describe where something they left at home is. Walk round the room and say what is where.
partnerEn: your flatmate, at work and asking for directions on the phone
openingEn: Can you have a look? I can't remember where I put my glasses.
goalEn: At least three places have been described, the thing being looked for has been found and where it was has been said in one clear sentence.

sceneEn: You are arranging your new room with a friend. They keep asking where to put the thing in their hands; you say where it goes each time.
partnerEn: a friend walking about with boxes who keeps asking
openingEn: I've still got the lamp here. Where shall I put it?
goalEn: Where at least three things go has been said, one has been moved afterwards and the room has been finished.

sceneEn: You have moved into your new place and you and a friend are furnishing a room. Argue about what goes where; disagree over one piece and come to a decision in the end.
partnerEn: a friend who wants a different arrangement from yours
openingEn: So, where does the desk go? By the window?
goalEn: Where at least three things go has been discussed, one disagreement has come up and a shared decision has been reached in the end.

sceneEn: Someone who has just moved into the area is asking you about the neighbourhood. Say what is where, where the nearest stop is and where you do your shopping.
partnerEn: a neighbour who has just moved into the area
openingEn: I've just moved in. Where do you do your shopping around here?
goalEn: At least three places have been described, the nearest stop has been named and the new neighbour knows where to go.

sceneEn: You are putting something together at home but you have not got the tool. Knock on your neighbour's door, ask for help, borrow a tool and say when you will bring it back.
partnerEn: a helpful but inquisitive neighbour
openingEn: Hello! Can I help you?
goalEn: Help has been asked for, a tool has been borrowed, a promise to return it has been made and thanks have been given.

sceneEn: A parcel for your neighbour has been left at your address. Knock on their door, say you took it in, say when it came and hand it over.
partnerEn: a surprised neighbour who has been waiting for the parcel
openingEn: Oh, hello! Do come in — has something happened?
goalEn: Why you have the parcel has been explained, it has been handed over and the neighbour has said thank you and offered something in return.

sceneEn: Your upstairs neighbour makes a lot of noise at night and you have not slept all week. Knock on their door, start politely, explain the problem and find a solution together.
partnerEn: an upstairs neighbour who has no idea they are making noise
openingEn: Hello, what's the matter? Is something not right?
goalEn: The problem has been raised politely, the neighbour has explained themselves and the two of you have agreed on something concrete.

sceneEn: Two things have broken at home and you are ringing the property management. Describe what is broken, say how long it has been like that and ask them to send someone.
partnerEn: a property manager taking notes on the phone
openingEn: Weber property management, good afternoon. What's broken at your place?
goalEn: Two faults have been described, a repair has been promised and the day and time have been agreed.

sceneEn: You have found a new job and met up with a friend. Talk about how you applied, how the interview went and what the job is like.
partnerEn: a friend who is looking for work themselves
openingEn: I hear you've got a new job. How's it going, then?
goalEn: The application, the interview and starting the job have been told in order, and you have given your friend a piece of advice.

sceneEn: On the first day of the language course the teacher is asking the class why they are learning German. Give your reason in a subordinate clause and say what you find hard.
partnerEn: a course teacher who wants to get to know the class
openingEn: Welcome! Do tell me: why are you learning German?
goalEn: At least two reasons have been given in subordinate clauses, one difficult point has been named and the teacher has given a piece of advice.

sceneEn: You are stuck in traffic and you will be late for work. Ring your colleague, say how late you will be and explain why.
partnerEn: a colleague waiting for you who will put the meeting back
openingEn: Hello? Where have you got to? We were going to start at nine.
goalEn: How late you will be and the reason have been given, and you and your colleague have decided what to do.

sceneEn: It is your first day in your new job. A colleague is showing you round the office and introducing you to people. Introduce yourself and ask who does what.
partnerEn: a helpful colleague showing you round the office
openingEn: Welcome to the team! Shall I show you the office first?
goalEn: You have introduced yourself, met at least two people and found out who does what.

sceneEn: You are in a team meeting talking about a new project. Give your opinion, make a suggestion and say whether you agree with someone else's.
partnerEn: a team leader chairing the meeting
openingEn: Before we start: what do you all think about the new project?
goalEn: An opinion has been given in a subordinate clause, a suggestion has been made and the team leader has reached a decision.

sceneEn: The phone is ringing in the office and the person being asked for is not there. Take the call, find out who is calling and what about, take the number and say you will pass the message on.
partnerEn: a customer trying to reach one of your colleagues
openingEn: Good afternoon, could I speak to Ms Keller, please?
goalEn: The caller's name, business and number have been taken and you have said the message will be passed on.

sceneEn: You and a colleague are deciding where to go on your lunch break. Say what you would prefer, give your reason and choose what to eat.
partnerEn: a colleague who is tired of going to the same place every day
openingEn: Shall we go to the canteen again, or somewhere else for once today?
goalEn: Where to go has been decided and you have both said what you are having.

sceneEn: You want to take leave in the summer but the team is busy at that time. Give your manager the dates, say how many days you want and suggest what should happen while you are away.
partnerEn: a manager looking at the holiday rota
openingEn: You wanted to talk about leave? When would you like to be off?
goalEn: The dates and the length of the leave have been given, one obstacle has been discussed and a date has been agreed in the end.

sceneEn: You have fallen ill in the morning and you are ringing the office to let them know. Say what is wrong, say how many days you will be off and discuss how you will send in the note.
partnerEn: someone from HR who has answered the phone
openingEn: Good morning, HR department. What can I do for you?
goalEn: The illness has been reported, the length has been given and it has been agreed when and how the note will arrive.

sceneEn: You are in your annual appraisal. Your manager is giving you feedback; say where you disagree and why, and put a request of your own politely.
partnerEn: a manager who speaks directly but listens
openingEn: Do sit down. How has this year been for you?
goalEn: The year has been reviewed, one point has been objected to with reasons, and a request has been made and answered.
